summary: Allocation collision detected before substantive Tele archaeology. Multiple append-only claims for the same job/dedupe_key became durable concurrently. This worker's claim at 2026-09-17T17:48:49Z is later than the durable 2026-09-17T17:48:37Z claim, so this worker yields and performs no duplicate project work.
tests: Post-claim directory read showed four durable claim files for job_id portfolio-tele-recover-intent-and-artifacts sharing dedupe_key tele:recover-intent-artifacts:v1.
Earliest observed durable claim has claimed_at 2026-09-17T17:48:37Z; this worker has claimed_at 2026-09-17T14:48:49-03:00 (=17:48:49Z), so this worker is not the earliest claimant.
No substantive Tele archaeology was executed after collision detection.
unresolved: Portfolio claim filenames are unique per claimant, so create-if-absent on those filenames does not itself provide dedupe-level mutual exclusion under simultaneous workers.
An authoritative single-winner lock/reservation or deterministic collision-resolution mechanism is still required before portfolio allocation can claim atomic exclusivity under contention.

spawn_candidates.title: Harden portfolio claim exclusivity under concurrent /wc workers
spawn_candidates.reason: A live four-way claim collision occurred for one portfolio job despite claim-before-work and dedupe requirements; the current append-only unique claim paths do not create a singleton lock.
acceptance: Two or more concurrent workers targeting the same portfolio dedupe_key cannot both become substantive execution owners.
A losing worker can deterministically discover the winner and immediately re-enter allocation without doing duplicate work.
Existing append-only claim evidence and lineage remain preserved.
A contention canary with at least five simultaneous claim attempts demonstrates exactly one execution owner and safe loser retries.
